title: frugal-routing-prefill-agents-and-quantize-presets
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Many tenants see unpredictable unit economics when cold bursts and skewed request distributions interact with batching and quant fallbacks. This change introduces a lightweight 'Frugal Routing' prefill agent that applies tenant-aware routing policies, conservative batch hints, and a compact set of quantization presets to reduce tail unit-costs without impacting median latency. The goal is to provide a safe default that tenants can opt into via the CLI or defaults config.

What this PR does: Adds an orchestration agent that synthesizes routing decisions (fast-path vs. frugal-path), emits batch/cache hints to the serving runtime, and exposes a compact quant profiles YAML for quick pilot rollouts. Includes: 1) econ/orchestrator service for real-time routing decisions, 2) a CLI dry-run simulator (cli/econ-sim) for tenants to model cost/latency tradeoffs on sample traces, 3) a small set of compact quant presets (q-presets/compact-low-latency.yaml) with documented safe fallbacks, 4) runbook and docs with rollout guidance and SLO knobs, 5) unit and integration tests and a smoketest for helm values.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced (Linear ENG-13421) - [x] Unit tests added and passing - [x] Integration dry-run CLI included - [x] Backwards compatible defaults (does not change existing tenant configs) - [x] Telemetry hooks added for cost/latency deltas

Rollout plan: Start as a tenant opt-in feature behind a feature flag. Run CLI dry-run for 48h on production traces, then enable for small tenant cohorts with telemetry gating (cost delta < 10% and latency P99 within SLO).

Notes on safety: The agent only issues hints (batch/cache/quant) and the serving runtime performs validation; quant presets include explicit degradation thresholds and automatic fallback to full-precision variants if coherence checks fail.

Related: touches cost tooling and prefill logic; see ENG-13456 for long-running monitoring integration.
